titulo: Simple and articulated prepositions: Di, a, da and in

aula.objetivo: Choose between «di», «a», «da» and «in», merge prepositions with articles («al», «nel», «sul», «dal», «del») and use «me» and «te» after prepositions. Avoid the English-speaker traps: word-for-word prepositions, «a il», and «in due ore».

blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: English prepositions do not match Italian ones one-to-one. English «in», «at», «on» and «to» cover places in a way that feels random, while Italian splits the ground differently. Learn them in blocks, with examples. STEP 2: «di» shows possession, origin and material: «il libro del professore» (the professor's book), «Sono di Roma» (I am from Rome), «un bicchiere di vino» (a glass of wine). STEP 3: «a» goes with cities and with fixed places: «Abito a Roma» (I live in Rome), «Sono a casa» (I am at home), «Vado a scuola in autobus». It also introduces a time: «alle otto». STEP 4: «da» means «from» when you say where you come from: «Vengo da Roma». It also means «at someone's place»: «Vado dal dottore» (I go to the doctor's). STEP 5: «in» goes with countries, regions and many enclosed or general places: «in Italia», «in autobus», «in ufficio». STEP 6: for means of transport, «in» works without an article: «in autobus», «in treno». «A piedi» (on foot) is the exception. STEP 7: contrast city and country: «Sono a Roma» (city) but «Sono in Italia» (country); «Sono a casa» (home) but «Sono in ufficio» (office). STEP 8: English «from» covers two ideas that Italian keeps apart: where you are originally from, «Sono di Roma» (I am from Rome), and where you are coming from right now, «Vengo da Roma» (I am coming from Rome).
blocos.comparacao: English «at the bar» and «to the bar» both become «al bar» in Italian. English «I come from Rome» uses «from», and Italian uses «da»: «Vengo da Roma», but «Sono di Roma» when you say where you are originally from. The learner's trap is translating the preposition word for word: «I go to school by bus» is not «Vado a la scuola con autobus». Use the whole block: «Vado a scuola in autobus».

exemplos.pt: I go to school by bus

tabela.exemplo: origin of motion; at someone's place

erros.motivo: To say where you are coming from, use «da».
English puts the owner first («the professor's book»). Italian puts the thing first and the owner after «di».

itens.explicacao: «Da» marks where you come from when you move.

itens.enunciado: Which preposition completes «Abito ___ Roma» (I live in Rome)?
Which preposition completes «Sono ___ Italia» (I am in Italy)?

blocos.enunciado: Say six sentences aloud about yourself: where you live (a/in), where you are from (di), how you travel (in), and a visit to someone (da).
Explain aloud why English «at» and «to» can both become one preposition in «al bar».
